Plot method for sparse_diss objects

Source: R/sparse_fit.R
plot.sparse_diss.Rd

plot method for objects of class sparse_diss. Shows the samples on two axes of a PCoA of the full dissimilarity matrix, with the selected pairs drawn as segments between samples.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sparse_diss'
plot(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  k = c(1, 2),
  edge_types = NULL,
  edge_col_by = "type",
  edge_alpha = 0.4,
  edge_linewidth = 0.3,
  add_points = TRUE,
  point_size = 1.5,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class sparse_diss, as returned by sparse_diss.

y

Currently unused.

k

Integer vector of length 2 indicating which PCoA axes to plot. Must be within the k_pcoa axes stored in x. Default is c(1, 2).

edge_types

Optional character vector with the type of pairs to draw (any of 'knn', 'random', 'zero'). Default is NULL (all).

edge_col_by

Character string: colour segments by pair 'type' (default) or by dissimilarity ('diss').

edge_alpha

Numeric transparency of segments. Default is 0.4.

edge_linewidth

Numeric width of segments. Default is 0.3.

add_points

Logical indicating whether to add the default sample points layer via ggplot2::geom_point(). Default is TRUE. Set to FALSE to omit it and add a custom one instead.

point_size

Numeric size of points. Default is 1.5.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A ggplot object, so that it can be further customised (e.g. plot(sp) + ggplot2::theme_bw()). The default data of the plot contains the PCoA coordinates of each sample, in columns PCoA.1 and PCoA.2 (the plotted axes, in order).

Details

The PCoA is computed on the full dissimilarity matrix, on the link scale (see k_pcoa and link in sparse_diss).
